purpose: Mesalamine is used to treat inflammatory bowel conditions like ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease. It helps reduce inflammation in your intestines and colon. It can help control flare-ups and keep your condition in remission so you feel better day to day.
how_it_works: Mesalamine works by calming down inflammation directly in the lining of your colon and intestines. Think of it like putting a soothing balm right where the irritation is happening. It blocks certain chemicals in your body that cause swelling and irritation in your gut.
common_side_effects: Some people may experience headache, nausea, stomach pain, diarrhea, or gas. You might also notice mild cramping or a runny nose. Most side effects are mild and tend to improve as your body adjusts to the medication.
warnings: In rare cases, mesalamine can affect your kidneys, so your doctor may check your kidney function with blood tests. Stop taking it and call your doctor right away if you have severe stomach pain, bloody diarrhea, fever, or a rash. Tell your doctor if you are allergic to aspirin or similar medications, since mesalamine is related to aspirin.
typical_dosing: Dosing depends on the form you are taking — pill, capsule, suppository, or enema. Oral forms are usually taken once or twice daily with food, often with a full glass of water. Suppositories or enemas are typically used at bedtime and inserted directly into the rectum. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your form and condition.
